summary: The root وَهَجَ (wahaja) describes fire burning or glowing intensely. It also refers to the sun's heat or a day/night being violently hot. The core meaning is intense heat or burning.
lane: 1 وَهَجَتِ النَّارُ ذ , aor. تَهِجُ , inf. n. وَهْجٌ and وَهَجَانٌ ; (S, L, K;) and وَهَجَتَ , [app. a mistake for وَهِجَت ,] aor. تَوْهَجُ , [inf. n. وَهَجٌ ;] (L;) The fire burned; syn. اِتَّقَدَت ; (S, K, &c.;) and so ; (L;) syn. توقّدت ; (S, L, K;) [or this last has an intensive sense, and signifies, as does the first accord. to the A, it burned fiercely; glowed ]. -b2- Also, all these verbs, with the same inf. ns., It (the sun) burned, or was hot: and it (a fire) burned from a distance. (L.) -b3- Also, all the above verbs, with the same inf. ns., (tropical:) It (a day, and a night,) was violently hot. (L.)
